it appears we restrict the number of actions that can run on a card. if 1 action is running and we try to start another one, it will even try to queue the message.

this is all super over engineered, nothing of this is needed, all of these restrictions need to be removed: use should be able to run multiple actions at the same time, even of the same type. keep it simple

import { CUSTOM_PROMPT_ACTION_ID, type ActionDefinition } from '../../../../data/action_types'
import type { ActionPromptPreparationStatus } from '../../../../services/actions/action_prompt_draft_service'

interface ActionPopupRunState {
    agentActive: boolean
    interactionReady: boolean
    runDisabledMessage: string | null
    runStatus: string
}

/** Applies popup run readiness rules to the current live prompt. */
export function actionPopupRunDisabled(
    action: ActionDefinition,
    runState: ActionPopupRunState,
    prompt: string,
    preparationStatus: ActionPromptPreparationStatus,
) {
    const sessionActive = runState.runStatus === 'queued'
        || runState.runStatus === 'running'
        || runState.runStatus === 'waitingForInput'

    return !!runState.runDisabledMessage
        || preparationStatus !== 'ready'
        || (action.id === CUSTOM_PROMPT_ACTION_ID && prompt.trim().length === 0)
        || (runState.agentActive && (
            !runState.interactionReady
            || prompt.trim().length === 0
        ))
        || (sessionActive && !runState.agentActive)
}

entries.content:
Doc written. `status: ready for implementation`. Original text kept intact.

Core finding: desktop already runs many actions per card without any guard. All restriction sits in renderer — `action_run_registry.ts` binds exactly one run store per `action + context`, so a second run of the same action steals the popup binding from the first.

Fix shape in doc: popup binds to a **runId** chosen by the conversation combobox, not to the action. Combobox gains an explicit **New conversation** entry plus one entry per live concurrent conversation. Registry keeps an array of live stores per binding. Run-disabled gate `(sessionActive && !agentActive)` deleted.

Per your answers, two things stay and are marked as deliberate non-removals: the mid-turn prompt queue, and the worktree preparation guard.

Two flags:
- Prompt drafts are keyed `actionId + context` today. Concurrent runs would share one text box, so the plan adds the runId to the draft key. Touches `ActionPromptDraftService` API and its call sites.
- Touch surface is wide: 14 popup components move from `useActionRunSelector(actionId, context)` to a runId-based hook.
